    Running a scenario in your tenant

    Live run (Preview): how it works and where the data goes

    What happens

    • You sign in to Microsoft with your own work account, through an app registration your organisation created for MGC.
    • Before each step, MGC tells you which permission the step needs and why. Microsoft then asks you to allow it, in its own window.
    • MGC sends the step’s requests to Microsoft Graph. Graph answers with what your account can already see.
    • MGC shows the answer here: a table, headline counts and the raw JSON.

    Where your data goes

    • From Microsoft Graph to this browser tab, and nowhere else.
    • MGC has no server. GitHub Pages only served the page file. It never sees your sign-in or your results.
    • No AI model is involved. MGC sends no analytics and no telemetry.
    • Results stay in this tab’s memory. Signing out or closing the tab deletes them. Export CSV saves a file on your computer, and only when you press it.
    • Your browser remembers your tenant and the app (client) ID, so you don’t have to type them again. MGC never stores your access token.

    What MGC can and can’t do

    • It can read, with delegated permissions, what your account can already see. Nothing more.
    • It can’t change, create or delete anything. A read-only guard checks every request before it is sent and blocks anything that could change data.
    • It never uses application permissions, so it can’t reach data your account can’t.

    One step, from Run to results

    GitHub Pages only served the page file. It never sees your access token or your results. There is no MGC server, and no AI model is involved.

    What crosses where

    Words used here

    Delegated permission
    The app acts as you. It can only reach what your account can reach, and only the kind of data the permission covers.
    Application permission
    The app acts as itself, with no one signed in, across the whole tenant. MGC never uses these.
    Consent
    Your approval, or an admin’s, for the app to use a permission. Microsoft asks for it in its own window.
    Access token
    A short-lived pass from Microsoft that lets this page call Microsoft Graph as you. MGC keeps it in this tab’s memory only.
    Read-only
    A request that only reads data. MGC sends GET requests, plus a few searches and checks that use POST but change nothing.
